body: Wild Arms XF is Media.Vision's PSP tactical role-playing game, first released in Japan on 9 August 2007. It takes the Wild Arms setting into battles fought by a small squad across hexagonal maps. Characters develop through classes whose skills can later be combined, making preparation closely connected to the problem presented by the next encounter. The player has to consider how the group moves around an enemy as well as the strength of its weapons. Position becomes a shared resource, giving a carefully arranged formation opportunities that isolated fighters cannot create.

Formation Arts reward particular arrangements around an enemy, while Combination Arts allow several allies to connect their attacks. The same advantages can be used by the opposition, so an apparently strong position has to be checked for the response it permits. Class development adds another layer: permanently learned skills can be equipped outside their original class, allowing a character to combine roles. The player gradually builds a squad capable of solving different maps, then has to place those capabilities where they can work together. The hexagonal grid makes that arrangement visually distinct from a conventional square battlefield.

Nobukazu Sato directed the game, with Akifumi Kaneko writing its story and a group of composers led by Masato Kouda supplying the score. Story characters can be joined by hired Drifters, giving more room to shape the squad. North American and European releases followed in 2008. The class system makes experimentation useful between battles, while the map rewards careful execution during them. Wild Arms XF therefore finds a tactical role for the series' setting, asking the player to express progress through the capabilities of a group rather than only the development of one central hero.
